docs.title: ThematOS
docs.text:
LDA topic modeling on tomotopy. ThematOS is a plain Python library; it also ships HyFI 2.0 config groups and workflows, so a training run, a parameter sweep, or an inference run can be started from the command line and recorded in a run manifest. The name comes from the Greek θέματος, "of the theme".

  • Documentation
  • Migrating from 0.x

ThematOS 1.0 drops the HyFI 1.x API. Pin thematos<1 to keep it.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
uv add thematos          # or: pip install thematos
pip install pyLDAvis     # optional: LDAvis HTML next to the other artifacts

Python 3.11 or newer. Stopwords come from lexikanon, which pulls in MeCab through fugashi; on Python 3.15 fugashi builds from source and needs the MeCab library (apt-get install libmecab-dev or brew install mecab).

docs.title: Use it as a library
docs.text:
from thematos.datasets import Corpus
from thematos.models import LdaModel

corpus = Corpus(data_file="news.parquet", text_col="tokens")  # or Corpus(data=dataframe)
model = LdaModel(output_dir="workspace/topic/model", seed=42, model_args={"k": 10})
model.train(corpus)  # trains and computes coherence; writes nothing
model.save()  # model file, log-likelihood trace, distributions, top words
model.summarize()  # tomotopy summary and one JSON line in model-summary.jsonl
model.plot()  # log-likelihood plot and topic word clouds
model.model.perplexity

Every file name starts with the model id, LDA_model_k(10) here. Importing thematos never imports HyFI.

docs.title: Use it from HyFI
docs.text:
Installing thematos registers its config groups through the hyfi.plugins entry point:

group options model lda dataset topic_corpus (stopwords from lexikanon's stopwords group) words wordprior plot wordcloud workflow thematos_lda, thematos_lda_sweep, thematos_lda_infer 
hyfi run workflow=thematos_lda dataset.data_file=news.parquet dataset.text_col=tokens \
  model.model_args.k=20 model.seed=42

Artifacts go under the project workspace (workspace/topic/model/ by default) and the run manifest under .hyfi/runs/<run id>/manifest.json. See Usage for the sweep and inference workflows.

docs.title: API reference
docs.text:
Workflow steps: small functions that chain a load, corpus, and model through HyFI steps:.

Each step returns what the next one takes as its first argument (HyFI pipe). They work the same when called from plain Python.

docs.title: Corpus
docs.text:
Bases: Model

Documents from a DataFrame (data) or a file (data_file), as a tomotopy corpus.

docs.title: load()
docs.text: Tokenize the documents (and concatenate n-grams) into a tomotopy corpus.

docs.title: TopicModel
docs.text:
Bases: Model

A topic model whose artifacts live under output_dir.

File names start with model_id (<MODEL_TYPE>_<name>_k(<k>)), so models that differ in name or k can share one directory.

docs.title: num_topics property
docs.text: Number of topics in the model

docs.title: model_summary_file property
docs.text: One JSON line per trained model, shared by every model in output_dir.

docs.title: train(corpus=None)
docs.text:
Train on corpus (or the one already set) and evaluate coherence.

Nothing is written; call :meth:save, :meth:summarize, and :meth:plot for artifacts.

docs.title: save()
docs.text: Write the model file, log-likelihood trace, distributions, and top words.

docs.title: summarize()
docs.text: Write the tomotopy summary and append this model's metrics to the summary jsonl.

docs.title: plot()
docs.text: Write the log-likelihood plot, topic word clouds, and LDAvis (if installed).

docs.title: load()
docs.text: Load the model file and saved distributions written by :meth:save for model_id.

docs.title: infer(corpus, output_file=None, iterations=100, tolerance=-1, num_workers=0, together=False)
docs.text: Infer topic distributions for corpus and save them (with log-likelihoods).

docs.title: build_corpus(data=None, *, corpus)
docs.text: Tokenize data (or corpus.data_file when no data is piped in) into corpus.

docs.title: train(corpus, *, model)
docs.text: Train model on corpus and save the model file and its distributions.

docs.title: sweep(corpus, *, model, k, alpha=None, eta=None)
docs.text:
Train, save, summarize, and plot one model per (k, alpha, eta) combination.

Models are named <name>(0), <name>(1), ... in sweep order, and every model's summary is appended to <output_dir>/model-summary.jsonl. Returns the summaries.

docs.title: infer(corpus, *, model, output_file=None, iterations=100, tolerance=-1, num_workers=0, together=False)
docs.text: Load model (as saved under its output_dir) and infer topics for corpus.

docs.title: Migrating from 0.x
docs.text:
ThematOS 1.0 runs on HyFI 2.0 and no longer imports HyFI itself. To stay on the old API, pin thematos<1 (which needs hyfi<2, lexikanon<1, and Python below 3.13).

0.x 1.0 from thematos import HyFI, thematos console command import hyfi only where you compose configs; the hyfi CLI TopicModel(BatchTask), Corpus(BatchTask) with task_name, batch_name, batch, path plain Pydantic models; LdaModel(output_dir=...) files under workspace/<task_name>/<batch_name>/{models,outputs} everything under output_dir (${project.workspace}/topic/model in the config) model id LDA_model(0)_k(5) from the batch number LDA_<name>_k(5); the sweep names models model(0), model(1), ... batch.seed (random when -1), batch.num_workers seed (random when null), num_workers save_config() / load(batch_num=...) the run manifest records the config; load() reads the files for the same output_dir, name, and k train() with autosave: true wrote every artifact train(corpus) writes nothing; chain .save().summarize().plot(), or use the workflow steps Corpus(data_load=...) (a HyFI load_dataframe run) Corpus(data_file=...) or Corpus(data=dataframe) corpus doc ids saved to corpus_doc_ids.parquet ids are in <id>-doc_topic_dists.parquet TopicRunner with calls: [train, infer], LdaRunConfig, InferConfig workflows thematos_lda_sweep and thematos_lda_infer (thematos.steps.sweep, thematos.steps.infer) runner/<name>_summaries.json model-summary.jsonl, one line per model groups model/config, model/train, model/summary, model/plot, ngrams, runner, about model_args, train_args, train_summary_args, and ngrams are inline in model=lda and dataset=topic_corpus; model/plot is plot=wordcloud /stopwords@stopwords: __init__ (lexikanon 0.x) /stopwords@stopwords: default (lexikanon 1.x) LdaConfig.k: null k: 10 generate_config() and other HyFI model helpers removed word cloud font picked by HyFI (lang) wc.font_path; wordcloud's default font when unset

Results did not change: with the same corpus, word priors, seed, and one worker, the tests reproduce the perplexity, coherence, and top words recorded with thematos 0.14.5 on hyfi 1.37.0 (tests/data/metrics_1x.json).

Fixed along the way:

  • tomotopy 0.14 renamed train(iter=) and infer(iter=) to iterations=; 1.0 requires tomotopy 0.14 or newer.
  • WordPrior.save() works when data_file does not exist yet.

docs.title: Library
docs.text:
Every class is a Pydantic model; construct it with keyword arguments. Unknown keys are errors.

class module what it does Corpus thematos.datasets tokenizes a text or token-list column into a tomotopy corpus, removes stopwords, concatenates frequent n-grams LdaModel thematos.models trains tomotopy.LDAModel, evaluates coherence, writes artifacts under output_dir WordPrior thematos.models seed words per topic, from a YAML/JSON file and/or prior_data WordCloud, WordcloudConfig thematos.plots, thematos.models word cloud settings for LdaModel.plot()

Corpus reads data_file (.parquet, .csv, or .jsonl) unless you pass a DataFrame as data. A column of token lists is joined with spaces before tokenizing, as in 0.x.

LdaModel needs an output_dir. Its methods return the model, so they chain:

method writes train(corpus) nothing; trains and evaluates coherence_metric_list save() <id>.mdl, <id>-ll_per_word.csv, <id>-doc_topic_dists.parquet, <id>-topic_term_dists.parquet, <id>-used_vocab.txt, <id>-topic_top_words.txt, <id>-topic_top_words_dists.csv summarize() <id>-summary.txt, one line in model-summary.jsonl (perplexity, coherence, arguments) plot() <id>-ll_per_word.png, wordclouds/<id>-wordcloud_NNN.png, wordcloud_collage/<id>_wordcloud_NN.png, <id>-ldavis.html (with pyLDAvis) load() reads back what save() wrote for the same output_dir, name, and k infer(corpus) inferred_topics/<id>-inferred_doc_topic_dists.parquet

The model id is <MODEL_TYPE>_<name>_k(<k>), for example LDA_model_k(10).

seed=None (the default) lets tomotopy draw a random seed. For a reproducible run set seed and keep num_workers=1: tomotopy's result depends on the number of workers.

docs.title: Config groups
docs.text:
option builds model=lda LdaModel with output_dir: ${project.workspace}/topic/model, words=wordprior as wordprior, plot=wordcloud as wc_args dataset=topic_corpus Corpus with lexikanon's stopwords=default and the 0.x n-gram settings words=wordprior WordPrior plot=wordcloud WordcloudConfig

The config files hold the same defaults as the classes. Every node has a _target_, so hyfi.instantiate builds the object:

import hyfi

model = hyfi.instantiate(hyfi.compose_group("model", "lda", ["model.model_args.k=20"]))

docs.title: Workflows
docs.text:
The functions in thematos.steps take the previous step's result as their first argument:

  • build_corpus(data, corpus=...): puts a DataFrame into the corpus and tokenizes it.
  • train(corpus, model=...): model.train(corpus).save().
  • summarize(model), plot(model): the model methods of the same name.
  • sweep(corpus, model=..., k=[...], alpha=[...], eta=[...]): one model per combination, named <name>(0), <name>(1), ...; each is saved, summarized, and plotted. Returns the summaries.
  • infer(corpus, model=..., iterations=100, ...): model.load(), then model.infer(corpus).

The example workflows put dataset and model at the root of the config, so overrides read dataset.<key>=... and model.<key>=...:

# one model: load -> build corpus -> train -> summarize -> plot
hyfi run workflow=thematos_lda dataset.data_file=news.parquet dataset.text_col=tokens model.seed=42

# a sweep over k; summaries land in workspace/topic/model/model-summary.jsonl
hyfi run workflow=thematos_lda_sweep dataset.data_file=news.parquet 'workflow.steps.2.with.k=[5,10,20]'

# topics for new documents, from the model the sweep saved as model(1)
hyfi run workflow=thematos_lda_infer dataset.data_file=new.parquet "model.name='model(1)'" model.model_args.k=10

Each run writes .hyfi/runs/<run id>/manifest.json with the resolved config, versions, git state, and per-step status. That record replaces the 0.x configs/model(N)_config.yaml files.

The steps build thematos.* and lexikanon.stopwords.Stopwords objects, so pass both when you limit targets:

hyfi run workflow=thematos_lda dataset.data_file=news.parquet --allow 'thematos.*' --allow 'lexikanon.*'
